title: Dicky Wells and Earle Warren as teachers
summary: Wells took him around; Earle Warren, a father and teacher, could bridge the generation gap.

blocks.x: It does. It also means Eddie Durham is as great as I say he is, and he is. So it was Eddie Durham in the trombones and Benny Morton and Dicky Wills. I wasn’t too close with Vic. Vic was kind of shy I betcha. And to get children into his inner circle, he liked to talk to musicians and adults. And so, and I had such a friendship with Dicky Wells that took me all around. Dicky is my meal ticket, my ace — and he was so brilliant. Dicky Wells was wise too but Eddie Durham was the genius and wrote all that stuff. And then Earle Warren led the reeds. And he was the one I was closest to, because he was the leader and he was a teacher and he was a father. He did something that — I don’t know how much teaching you do but he did something with young people that I’m still trying to do, much less do as well. He’s the only one I’ve ever seen do this. I talk with Wynton Marsalis a lot about this because he doesn’t know — he knows Earle Warren but didn’t realize that if he led the reeds in that band he must be great. And I was asleep on him, so tell me about him. You know so like that’s really my function. I hung out with Earle Warren for 35 years and you get to hear about it because you can. That’s the formula. That’s why this is such a great thing that’s going on. If any of this is great and if I can convey it well or suitably. But Earle Warren’s most amazing talent to me — independent © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

of his musical greatness — was that you know adolescents are rebellious. They’re not necessarily political or socially oriented. I mean I think the youth movement concept is a little bit overrated. It happened in my generation in America and perhaps even internationally but it doesn’t always happen. But rebelliousness and fighting off the direction and wisdom, pontifications of the elder generation, that battle ground has been around, according to Aristotle, at least 3000 years, and Earle Warren is the only person who when it’s a cold line in the dirt, you’re on that side and I’m on this side, you’re the young person and Earle Warren, and he could say “listen I understand where you’re coming from, let me explain this to you.” And do it. And explain it so that everything calms down and that he could explain to the student or youngster why they were wrong, get them to accept it, to understand that it wasn’t just some browbeating coming down from on high, and to adapt it in some way, to synthesize it. And I’ve never seen anyone do it as well as Earle Warren did it. Absolutely outstanding ability to explain a complete difference of opinion over a generation gap and win — it’s not a competition, he knew that — to explain it. And to find common ground and good action from both sides.
